xof_many reads output-block count from SysV stacked seventh argument at RSP+8. Unsigned count>1 branches to vector setup; count0 and1 both enter scalar path and write64 bytes. Source establishes zero-count behavior at this entry, but public reachability and allocation contract require caller audit; no runtime overwrite reproduced.

For count>1, function saves RBP, reserves0x90 bytes and aligns stack64. Sixteen counters start from scalar counter plus offsets0..15, with unsigned low32 carry into high32 words. No increment-disable mask: output-block counters always advance across lanes.

Sixteen-output-block core broadcasts one common64-byte message into ZMM16..31 and CV into ZMM0..7, rather than reading16 distinct messages as hash-many does. Length and flags broadcast from EDX/R8d in this path. Caller extension contract remains separate from scalar byte-extension behavior.
Vector XOF core only partially read through3100: output transpose/stores, counter advances, smaller groups and constant tables remain unread.
